title: VQ-LLM: High-performance Code Generation for Vector Quantization Augmented LLM Inference
problem: Vector quantization (VQ) achieves higher compression ratios than element-wise quantization for LLM weights and KV cache (down to 1-2 bits), but existing VQ kernel implementations are slower than FP16 baselines due to two root causes: inefficient codebook access (excessive shared memory usage, bank conflicts, poor L1 hit rate at 12.45%) and uncoordinated dataflow between codebook loading and subsequent GEMM/attention computation (duplicated off-chip loads and shared-memory-to-register layout mismatches).
motivation: LLMs are heavily memory-bound and VQ can compress weights/KV-cache more aggressively than element-wise INT4, but without efficient GPU kernels the memory savings cannot translate to latency improvements, making VQ impractical despite its accuracy advantage.
method: VQ-LLM solves codebook access bottlenecks by placing the most frequently-used codebook entries in each thread's registers (avoiding slow shared-memory collisions), less common entries in shared memory, and rare ones in main memory. Instead of spreading lookups across many parallel paths that duplicate work, it reorganizes computation so each thread block loads exactly one codebook section at a time, then uses register shuffles (shfl.xor instructions) to pass data between threads without returning to shared memory. The system adaptively tunes its memory layout and work division by measuring shuffle overhead versus shared-memory latency for each vector-quantization configuration and GPU type.
key_novelty: VQ-LLM treats the codebook lookup as the center of its computation strategy: it places frequently-accessed codebook entries in registers, reorganizes work to load each codebook together as a unit, and uses register shuffles for inter-thread sharing—converting vector quantization from a speed bottleneck into a practical speedup over element-wise quantization.
contributions: Profiling analysis identifying two root causes of VQ kernel inefficiency: codebook placement causing shared-memory pressure/bank-conflicts, and uncoordinated dataflow causing redundant global-to-shared traffic and layout-mismatch shared-to-register traffic
Codebook cache abstraction with offline frequency-based hierarchical entry placement across registers/shared/global memory with lightweight reorder-based static mapping (no tag array needed)
Codebook-centric dataflow that parallelizes along codebook-switch axes with adaptive split factor to eliminate duplicate codebook loads
Register-level hierarchical fusion using GPU intra-warp shuffle to bypass shared memory for dequantized-to-compute layout rearrangement
64.36% to 99.1% latency reduction over open-source VQ implementations; competitive with AWQ and QoQ at equivalent bit-widths

metrics.speedup: 64.36% to 99.1% latency reduction vs open-source VQ implementations
metrics.other: Competitive with AWQ and QoQ at equivalent bit-widths on RTX 4090 and A40

limitations: Codebook frequency profiling is done offline per model/hardware combination; runtime changes in access patterns (e.g., different batch sizes or sequence lengths) may require re-profiling.
primary_theme: codebook-cache-centric GPU kernel generation for vector-quantized LLM inference
